opportunity: A call argument narrower than int that the caller zero-extends (movzx edi,di; movzbl) is trimmed to its narrow value, and C's integer promotion then widens the printed argument again: `sink(a0 * 3)` passes the untruncated product where the binary passes zext16(a0 * 3), and `sink(*(char *)(a0 + 3))` sign-extends a byte the binary zero-extends. Upstream Ghidra 12.1 prints the same `sink(param_1 * 3)`.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-truncarg.xml (10 assertions; #1-#4 and #8 fail on main, #10 fails with c_range disabled) + tests/stages/kuna-endptrbound.xml #5 (legitimate change) + docs/features/truncarg/roundtrip/roundtrip.sh (compile-and-run)
change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only adds the conversion the binary performs)
root_cause: ActionDeadCode counts only minimalmask(nzmask) of an unlocked call input as consumed, so RDI = ZEXT(x & 0xffff) consumes 0xffff; RuleSubvarAnd's SubvariableFlow then trims the call input to the 2-byte value through tryCallPull (nothing outside the mask is consumed). ActionSetCasts' default getInputCast compares the unlocked parameter's local type (undefined2) with the argument and asks for no cast, so a sub-int arithmetic argument prints bare and C promotes it. Found with an instrumented throwaway build printing the p-code after every changing rule/action (subvar_and is the step that replaces CALL sink,RDI:8 with CALL sink,DI:2). For a byte the trim leaves TYPE_UNKNOWN, a second cause: upstream's localExtensionType treats TYPE_UNKNOWN as zero-extending, but realtypes prints a one-byte unknown as `char`, which C sign-extends, so the promotion check and the printed C disagreed.
fix: p9_emit/kuna_truncarg.rs (narrowed_arg_cast), consulted by the default getInputCast arm when cast_standard asks for nothing: a CALL/CALLIND input narrower than sizeof(int), integer/unknown-typed and not an enum, whose slot no declared prototype type-locks, gets a cast to the unsigned integer of its width unless its promoted C value is already the zero-extension (int_promotion_type for an expression; the natural extension of the printed type for a variable, load or cast; a ZEXT always) or the expression's C value provably lies in [0, 2^(8*size)) (c_range over sign-clear constants, truth values and + * & | ^). The promotion check runs through FuncdataCastContext::with_unknown_byte_as, which reports a non-constant one-byte TYPE_UNKNOWN as int1 when ArchContext::unknown_byte_is_char (realtypes on, C output). An argument already printed as a truncating SUBPIECE cast, every read of which is a call argument, is retyped instead of double-cast (retype_truncation).

notes: Zero-extension is the right conversion for every narrowed input: the trim fires only when the dropped bits are known zero (non-aggressive tryCallPull consume test) or unread by the callee (RulePiecePathology), and the one sign-extension trim path (RuleSubvarSext aggressive_ext_trim) is off. A `char` is cast even on targets whose char is unsigned (arm32): C leaves char's signedness to the implementation, and the cast is right under either. The redundant casts are the price of deciding at the call site without the callee's prototype; a locked prototype suppresses the cast (stage assertion #7). Still open, named in 09-emission.md: the same trim at the promotion width (`sink64(a0 * 3)` with int a0, trimmed from RDI = ZEXT(EDI)) is converted by C with sign extension against an 8-byte callee; casting there would touch nearly every int argument on x86-64.
